anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have both GND1 and GND2 pins connected to the same common GND net.
anomalies.expected: For an isolated CAN transceiver, GND1 (controller side) and GND2 (bus side) must remain separate isolated grounds; the specification describes two isolated CAN buses implemented through isolated CAN transceivers.

Interface_CAN_LIN:ISO1050DUB | Isolated CAN Transceiver, SOP-8 | pins: 1=VCC1(power_in) 2=RXD(output) 3=TXD(input) 4=GND1(power_in) 5=GND2(power_in) ...
two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (`U8`, `U9`) through an isolated CAN transceiver (`U11`/companion)

anomalies.impact: Shorting GND1 and GND2 defeats the galvanic isolation of the CAN transceivers, potentially creating ground loops, reducing noise immunity, and exposing the CM4/CAN-controller side to bus-side ground faults or transients.

parsed.summary: The design files show a clear deviation from the specified isolated CAN architecture: both isolated CAN transceivers have their separate GND1/GND2 pins tied together on the common GND net, which removes the intended isolation.
